#### Foreword
###### This document specifies normative application-level requirements for S-Mode HVAC applications.

 This document builds on the existing HVAC specifications in Volume 7 and adds additional concepts and requirements.

 This document and possible further versions and other S-Mode HVAC application documents will substitute the “HVAC ObIS” specifications in Part 7/19 “HVAC ObIS” of the KNX Specifications.

#### Applicability of the proposed specification – transitional period

###### New products implementing functionality that is covered by these Application Specifications shall comply with the included requirements if submitted to KNX registration five years after the publication of the Approved Standard version. 

 Reassessed certified products of which the hardware and/or the applications are modified (updated, bug fixes, …) but implementing functionality that is covered by these Application Specifications shall comply with the include requirements if submitted to KNX registration five years after the publication of the Approved Standard version.


-----

### 1 Introduction

#### 1.1 Objectives
###### This document is part of the KNX HVAC Application Interworking Standard. The goal of this document is to specify the requirements for S-Mode HVAC applications for heating and cooling.

 Parts 7/11 “Hot Water Heating” and 7/13 “Terminal Unit Functional Blocks” define the common KNX application model for heating and cooling. The S-Mode requirements base on this and add additional requirements.

 This document 7/19/20 “S-Mode Heating and Cooling” specifies the requirements for S-Mode applications for heating and cooling.

 It repeats the FBs and DPs that shall be used in S-Mode.

 It also combines FBs of Part 7/10 7/11, 7/13 and 7/14 into single FBs in this paper.

 - This reduces the possible combinations of FBs in S-Mode which otherwise will lead to missing functionality and lack of (a wanted level of) Interworking.
 - These combinations are closer to the commonly implemented commercial realisations.

EXAMPLE 1 User Fan Speed Setting (UFS) is very often combined in the same product as the User HVAC
Room Settings (UHRS).

###### - S-Mode does not use the semantic information from the sender. The Inpus and Outputs are linked by the (user of the) S-Mode MaC the Input application may assume that the data is provided by the correct sender, without knowing and verifying its identity.

 It adds FB Profiles and Combined FB Profiles, to indicate which flavours of FBs and of combinations of FBs in an S-Mode product are allowed.

#### 1.2 Scope
###### This specification covers the following functionality.

 - Sensor FBs
 - HMI FBs
 - Actuator FBs
 - Room Temperature Controller
 - Room Temperature Setpoint Controller

 This specification does not cover the following functionality. That will be handled in the next versions.

 - Burner / Boiler
 - Pump / Mixer
 - Heat Distribution
 - Solar
 - Meter
 - Electrical Heating
 - Air quality
 - Humidity
 - Domestic Hot Water Control


-----

#### 1.3 Interworking Model
###### The KNX S-Mode HVAC Interworking is guaranteed through the standardisation and mandatory use of the following specifications.

 • Datapoint Type
 The mandatory format, encoding, range and unit of how any given data shall be communicated. For the same information, no other formats or encodings are allowed.

 • Functional Blocks (FBs)
 The elementary building block of the distributed application model. The functionality and interfaces of the FBs define how the distributed application model shall be built up.

 Any realisation of S-Mode HVAC functionality in a device shall respect the functionality of the referred FBs.

 The FBs are specified further in this document.

 • Functional Block Profiles (FB Profiles)
 The minimal requirements for the allowed combinations of Datapoints (DPs) and functionality in a Functional Block.

 Any realisation of a FB in an S-Mode HVAC functionality in a device shall at least comply with the minimal requirement of one FB Profile. 

 Not all FB definitions define FB Profiles: if no FB Profiles are defined for a FB, then this means that solely the indications of the mandatory – and optional DPs are sufficient for guaranteeing the Interworking and the implementation shall only comply with these M/O indications.

 The FB Profiles – if any are defined – are part of the FB specifications further in this document.

 • Combined Functional Block Profiles
 Combined Functional Block Profiles are minimal requirements for the allowed combinations of FBs in a device. A Combined FB Profile specifies which combinations of FBs shall be implemented in S-Mode HVAC applications. The gives FBs shall not be combined in another way, in order to guarantee Interworking.

 The defined and allowed Combined FB Profiles are specified in clause 2 “Combined FB Profiles” below.

#### 1.5 Use cases

##### 1.5.1 Conventions in the below specifications
###### 1 CU denotes “Control Unit”. It is the interface of this closed application towards any further application or level, like a scheduler, time clock, a BMS or other. Therefore, the DPs that give this interface are mentioned described and labelled, but the Control Unit as such is not defined.

 2 The RTC foresees interface for at maximum 4 different actuators: ActTargetPosHeatStageA, ActTargetPosHeatStageB, ActTargetPosCoolStageA and ActTargetPosCoolStageB. These are designed and shall be used for heat and cool staging. For the purpose of controlling multiple actuators of the same stage in parallel however, the integrator can connect these actuators to the single output, using the multicast aspect of KNX to control these actuators in parallel.

EXAMPLE 2 If the integrator realizes a heat stage A through 4 different radiators, then these may be 4 instances of the FB HVA, which are linked via the same Group
Address to the single ActTargetPosHeatStageA.

###### Especially for synchronisation of multiple HMIs (means multiple FBs ‘UHRS’) the FBs RTSM, RTC and HVA shall generate a lot of feedback information. This information shall be sent to UHRS with DPs as combined status information.

 The following information flow is necessary.

### 2 Combined FB Profiles

#### 2.1 Introduction

##### 2.1.1 Definition
###### It is necessary that any chosen combination of commercial devices Interworks in all implemented functionality. Therefore, Datapoints and Datapoint Types cannot be selected in any possible combination; instead, KNX HVAC S-Mode applications shall comply with the below specified Combined FB Profiles. This limits the product diversity and reduces the confusion to the user.

 If more than one FB is combined in a device, then direct interfaces become hidden. In the Combined FB Profiles, these interfaces can be made available externally in parts or complete.

 The internal FBs can be disabled. This makes the internal interfaces exposed again.

 Nevertheless, all Functional Blocks can combined in one device with available interfaces.

##### 2.1.2 Allowed Combined FB Profiles

###### 2.1.2.1 Overview

 • FBs UHRS, RTSM, RTC, HVA and FA The FBs UHRS, RTSM, RTC and HVA or FA shall at least be combined in the following combinations A to F as defined in Table 1.

 The column “Combined FB Profile” is relevant for the developer: it defines which combinations of FBs are allowed. Other combinations shall not be implemented. This shall add to guaranteeing that only devices are made available that can be combined to build a functioning application.

 The column “Possible Interworking” is not relevant for the developer: it shows how in an installation, the Combined FB Profile x can be linked to one or more other Combined FB Profiles to make a functioning application.

 The column “Possible extensions” is again relevant for the developer: is shows what further Combined FB Profiles are allowed to be implemented together with the given FB Profile. 

EXAMPLE 3 If the Combined FB Profile includes the UHRS (which is as stand-alone the Combined FB Profile E),
then this UHRS (E) can be implemented also more than once in the device. A can thus be extended with E and F, and this
makes that in turn, A can be an extension of E and F.
EXAMPLE 4 If the Combined FB Profile includes the HVA (which is as stand-alone the Combined FB Profile F),
then this HVA (F) can be implemented also more than one in the device. B can thus be extended with E, which makes that
E can be extended with B.

EXAMPLE 5 In a combination B (UHRS, RTSM and RTC) an RTS (Room Temperature Setpoint) may be
combined.

### 3 Sensor Functional Blocks

#### 3.1 FB Room Temperature Sensor (RTS)

##### 3.1.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block ‘Room Temperature Sensor’ measures the room temperature and delivers the data to the bus / system.

 This Functional Block is used e.g., in a ‘Room Temperature Sensor Device’ or in a more complex device that has the room temperature sensor functionality.

##### 3.1.2 Existing FBs

###### • Room Temperature Sensor (RTS) (Chapter 7/10/1 [01] clause 3.3)

##### 3.1.3 Functional specification
###### The distribution of the room temperature in the system is event-driven (COV-condition, change of value) and in addition repeated periodically.

 Optional feature

 - The sensor value may be corrected by a parameter value.

##### 3.1.4 Contraints
###### None.

###### 3.1.7.2 Output StatusGO

DP Name: StatusGO Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTS
**Description**
This Output contains the Z8 status information as a Group Object.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_StatusGen
DPT Format: B8 DPT_ID: 21.001
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
Status Z8 Status information Bitset
OutOfService (sensor is out of service) O Bit 0 t/f false
Fault (sensor value is corrupted) O Bit 1 t/f false
Overridden (sensor value is overridden) O Bit 2 t/f false
InAlarm (sensor is in alarm) O Bit 3 t/f false
AlarmUnAcknowledged O Bit 4 t/f false
reserved NA Bit 5-7 false
**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: none MinRepTime: 10 s
Cyclic Period: 15 min (recommended value)
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
None.

###### 3.1.7.3 Parameter TempHeartbeat

**FB:** **RTS** **Property Name (Server):** **TempHeartbeat** Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
The time duration for retransmission of the sensor value if no COV condition occurred before.
If this Parameter TempHeartbeat is not implemented, then the default value of 900 s shall be used.
**DPT:** Name DPT_TimePeriodSec DPT ID 7.005 Datatype format U16
Field Description Sup. Range Unit Default
Time period Period for latest retransmission of [0, MinRepTime ... 65 535] s 900
sensor value

**Communication:**

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 321 (RTS) Property ID: 115
**(in the server)** Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

**Property access:** Read only Read/Write
**Protection** Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

###### 3.1.7.4 Parameter TempMinRepTime

**FB:** **RTS** **Property Name (Server):** **TempMinRepTime** Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
Time duration for earliest retransmission of the sensor value even if the COV condition occurred before.
If this Parameter is not implemented, then the default value of 10 s shall be used.
**DPT:** Name DPT_TimePeriodSec DPT ID 7.005 Datatype format U16
Field Description Sup. Range Unit
Time period Period for earliest retransmission of M [0 ... Heartbeat] [1)] s
sensor value

**Communication:**

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 321 (RTS) Property ID: 116
**(in the server)** Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

**Property access:** Read only Read/Write
**Protection** Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
1) 0 = no minimum repetition time (not recommended when using small COV condition); minimum

repetition time greater than Heartbeat not applicable

#### 3.2 FB Floor Temperature Sensor (FTS)

##### 3.2.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block ‘Floor Temperature Sensor’ shall measure the floor temperature and deliver the data to the bus / system.

 This Functional Block is used e.g., in a ‘Floor Temperature Sensor Device’ or in a more complex device that has the floor temperature sensor functionality.

##### 3.2.2 Existing FBs

###### • Floor Temperature Sensor (FTS) (Chapter 7/10/1 [01] clause 3.26)

##### 3.2.3 Functional specification
###### The distribution of the floor temperature in the system is event-driven (COV-condition, change of value) and in addition repeated periodically.

 Optional feature

 - The sensor value may be corrected by a parameter value.

##### 3.2.4 Contraints
###### None.

**FTS**
**Inputs** **Outputs**

TempMinRepTime

###### 3.2.7.2 Output StatusGO

DP Name: StatusGO Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: FTS
**Description**
This Output contains the Z8 status information as a Group Object.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_StatusGen
DPT Format: B8 DPT_ID: 21.001
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
Status Z8 Status information Bitset
OutOfService (sensor is out of service) O Bit 0 t/f false
Fault (sensor value is corrupted) O Bit 1 t/f false
Overridden (sensor value is overridden) O Bit 2 t/f false
InAlarm (sensor is in alarm) O Bit 3 t/f false
AlarmUnAcknowledged O Bit 4 t/f false
reserved NA Bit 5-7 false
**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: none MinRepTime: 10 s
Cyclic Period: 15 min (recommended value)
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
None.

###### 3.2.7.3 Parameter TempHeartbeat

**FB:** **FTS** **Property Name (Server):** **TempHeartbeat** Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
The time duration for retransmission of the sensor value if no COV condition occurred before.
If this Parameter TempHeartbeat is not implemented, then the default value of 900 s shall be used.
**DPT:** Name DPT_TimePeriodSec DPT ID 7.005 Datatype format U16
Field Description Sup. Range Unit Defaul

t
Time period Period for latest retransmission of [0, MinRepTime ... 65535] s 900
sensor value

**Communication:**

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 329 (FTS) Property ID: 115
**(in the server)** Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

**Property access:** Read only Read/Write
**Protection** Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

###### 3.2.7.4 Parameter TempMinRepTime

**FB:** **FTS** **Property Name (Server):** **TempMinRepTime** Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
Time duration for earliest retransmission of the sensor value even if the COV condition occurred before.
If this Parameter is not implemented, then the default value of 10 s shall be used.
**DPT:** Name DPT_TimePeriodSec DPT ID 7.005 Datatype format U16
Field Description Sup. Range Unit
Time period Period for earliest retransmission of M [0 ... Heartbeat] [1)] s

#### 3.3 FB Outside Temperature Sensor (OTS)

##### 3.3.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block ‘Outside Temperature Sensor’ shall measure the outside air temperature and deliver the data to the bus / system.

 This Functional Block is used e.g., in a ‘Outside Temperature Sensor Device’ or in a more complex device that has the outside temperature sensor functionality.

##### 3.3.2 Existing FBs

###### • Outside Temperature Sensor (OTS) (Chapter 7/10/1 ([01]) clause 3.2)

##### 3.3.3 Functional specification
###### The distribution of the outside temperature in the system is event driven. (COV-condition, change of value) and in addition repeated periodically.

 Optional feature

 - The sensor value may be corrected by a parameter value.

##### 3.3.4 Contraints
###### None.

###### 3.3.7.2 Output StatusGO

DP Name: StatusGO Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: OTS
**Description**
This Output contains the Z8 status information as a Group Object.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_StatusGen
DPT Format: B8 DPT_ID: 21.001
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
Status Z8 Status information Bitset none
Bit 0 OutOfService O t/f
Bit 1 Fault O t/f
Bit 2 Overridden O t/f
Bit 3 InAlarm O t/f
Bit 4 AlarmUnAcknowledged O t/f
Bits 5...7 reserved NA
**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: none MinRepTime: 10 s
Cyclic Period: 15 min (recommended value)
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
None.

###### 3.3.7.3 Parameter TempHeartbeat

**FB:** **OTS** **Property Name (Server):** **TempHeartbeat** Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
The time duration for retransmission of the sensor value if no COV condition occurred before.
If this Parameter TempHeartbeat is not implemented, then the default value of 900 s shall be used.
**DPT:** Name DPT_TimePeriodSec DPT ID 7.005 Datatype format U16
Field Description Sup. Range Unit Default
Time period Period for latest retransmission of [0, MinRepTime ... 65535] s 900
sensor value

**Communication:**

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 320 (OTS) Property ID: 115
**(in the server)** Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

**Property access:** Read only Read/Write
**Protection** Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

###### 3.3.7.4 Parameter TempMinRepTime

**FB:** **RTS** **Property Name (Server):** **TempMinRepTime** Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
Time duration for earliest retransmission of the sensor value even if the COV condition occurred before.
If this Parameter is not implemented, then the default value of 10 s shall be used.
**DPT:** Name DPT_TimePeriodSec DPT ID 7.005 Datatype format U16
Field Description Sup. Range Unit
Time period Period for earliest retransmission of M [0 ... Heartbeat] [1)] s
sensor value

**Communication:**

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 321 (RTS) Property ID: 116
**(in the server)** Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

**Property access:** Read only Read/Write
**Protection** Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
1) 0 = no minimum repetition time (not recommended when using small COV condition); minimum

repetition time greater than Heartbeat not applicable

Field Description Sup. Range Unit
FloatValue Temperature COV value M Full Range K
**Communication:**

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 320 (OTS) Property ID: None.

**Property access:** Read only Read/Write
**Protection** Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

#### 3.4 FB Dew Point Status Sensor (DPS)

##### 3.4.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block ‘Dew Point Status Sensor’ shall acquire the dew point status and provide it to the system.

##### 3.4.2 Existing FBs

###### • Dew Point Status Sensor (DPS) (Chapter 7/10/1 ([01]) clause 3.24)

##### 3.4.3 Functional specification
###### The distribution of the DewPointStatus in the system is event driven (COV-condition, change of value) and in addition repeated periodically.

 The information is transmitted spontaneously at each change.

##### 3.4.4 Contraints
###### None.

**DPS**

DewPointStatus[RTC, UHRS]►

**Additional I/Os** **Parameters**

Heartbeat

###### 3.4.7.2 Parameter Heartbeat

**FB:** **DPS** **Property Name (Server):** **Heartbeat** Mandatory

#### 3.5 FB Window Switch (WOS)

##### 3.5.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block “Window Switch” shall acquire the status of one or several windows in a room and provide the result to the bus.

 This Functional Block is used e.g., in a ‘Window Switch Device’ or in a more complex device that has the window switch functionality.

 No cascading of window switches is defined in WOS. If multiple WOS are combined, multiple inputs in the RTSM should be implemented.

##### 3.5.2 Existing FBs

###### • Window Switch (WS) (Chapter 7/10/1 ([01]) clause 3.11)

##### 3.5.3 Functional specification
###### The distribution of the WindowStatus in the system is event driven (COV-condition, change of value).

 The Output ‘WindowStatus’ is delayed (e.g., 10 s) in order to prevent from toggling. (See description below.) This information is used in the ‘Room Temperature Setpoint Manager’.

##### 3.5.4 Contraints
###### None.

###### 3.5.7.2 Parameter Heartbeat

**FB:** **WOS** **Property Name (Server):** **Heartbeat** Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
The time duration for retransmission of the window status if no COV condition occurred before.
**DPT:** Name DPT_TimePeriodSec DPT ID 7.005 Datatype format U16
Field Description Sup. Range
Time period Period for latest retransmission of [0, MinRepTime ... 65535] [a] s
sensor value

**Communication:**

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 343 (WOS) Property ID: 115
**(in the server)** Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

**Property access:** Read only Read/Write
**Protection** Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

#### 3.6 FB Presence Detector (PRD)

##### 3.6.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block ‘Presence Detector’ shall acquire the presence status and provide it to the system.

 This Functional Block is used e.g., in a ‘Presence Detector Device’, in a ‘Presence Detector Switch Device’ or in a more complex device that has the presence detector functionality.

##### 3.6.2 Existing FBs

###### • Presence Detector (PRD) (Chapter 7/10/1 ([01]) clause 3.12)

##### 3.6.3 Functional specification
###### The distribution of the PresenceStatus in the system is event driven (COV-condition, change of value) and in addition repeated periodically.

 The presence status e.g., can be acquired by means of a sensor (automatic), described here or by means of a switch (manual).

 The information is transmitted spontaneously at each change.

##### 3.6.4 Contraints
###### None.

#### 3.7 Water Change Over Status Sensor (WCOS)

##### 3.7.1 Aims and objectives
###### This Functional Block is not part of the room heating and cooling application as specified in this document; it is part of the heat and cold production and distribution. It is only documented for completeness. For the the full understanding of the DPs in this FB that link to those functions, please refer to Volume 7.

 The Functional Block ‘Water Change Over Status Sensor’ acquires the temperature/status of the water, supplied e.g., to the fancoil and provides the information ‘Heating’ or ‘Cooling’ to the system.

 This Functional Block is used e.g., in a 'Water Change Over Status Sensor Device' or in a more complex device that contains this functionality.

 The temperature/status may be acquired internal (hardwired sensor) or via BUS. In case of status acquisition via BUS, the Functional Block transforms an ‘ON/OFF’ information to the ‘Heating’ / ‘Cooling’ information. An additional Input offers a manual change of the change over mode. This Input is used for manual override of the detected status.

##### 3.7.2 Functional Specification
###### The distribution of the ChangeOverStatus in the system is event driven (COV-condition, change of value) and in addition repeated periodically.

 The Output information is ‘Heating’ or ‘Cooling’. In case of a temperature measurement, the level values may be set with parameters, in case of a switch the switch interpretation (normally open or normally closed) can be set.

 Optional functions:

 - Faults in the sensor may be detected and reported.
 - The status value may temporary be overridden by means of a tool for service purpose.
 - The ‘Overridden’ condition must be reported.

 Inputs

 • TempFlowWater This Input takes the temperature from a sensor. By means of the parameters the Functional Block defines the change over status.

 This Input is used alternatively with the switch.

 • ChangeOverSwitch This Input takes the information from a normal switch.

 The relation on/off to heating/cooling may be defined by means of a parametrer. Binding only is possible in the Standard Mode.

 This Input is used alternatively with the temperature.

 • ChangeOverMode This Input receives the information from a HMI (e.g., switch) which is operated by e.g., a person who is responsible for the heating/cooling. This Input has higher priority than the others. In the position AUTO the Input of the other Inputs is valid.

 Outputs This Output delivers the information heating or cooling to the controllers, in order to change the controller sequence.

 ChangeOverStatus


-----

###### Parameters

 TempHeatingLevel If the temperature of the sensor is higher than this value, then the Functional Block delivers heating to the system.

 TempCoolingLevel If the temperature of the sensor is lower than this value, then the Functional Block delivers cooling to the system.

 SwitchDefinitionHeat/Cool Company specific definition of the relation between the hardware switch position and the bus information.

 Heartbeat This parameter defines the time duration for periodical retransimission of the sensor value if no COV condition change of the Change Over Status) occurred before.

 MinRepTime This parameter defines the time duration for earliest retransmission of the sensor value even if the COV condition occurred before.

##### 3.7.3 Constraints
###### The Input ‘ChangeOverSwitch’ can only be used in the S-Mode as a corresponding switch is not defined.

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 342 (WCOS) Property ID: 113
**(in the server)** Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

###### 3.7.6.8 Parameter Heartbeat

**FB:** **WCOS Property Name (Server):** **Heartbeat** Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**

The time duration for retransimission of the sensor value if no COV condition occurred before.
**DPT:** Name DPT_TimePeriodSec DPT ID 7.005 Datatype format U16
Field Description Sup. Range
Time period Period for latest retransmission of [0, MinRepTime ... 65535] [1)] s
sensor value

**Communication:**

**DP Address:** IO Type(ID): 342 (WCOS) Property ID: 115
**(in the server)** Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

**Property access:** Read only Read/Write
**Protection** Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
--**Special Features:**
1) 0 = no heartbeat; heartbeats smaller than MinRepTime not applicable

### 4 HMI Functional Blocks

#### 4.1 FB User HVAC Room Settings (UHRS)

##### 4.1.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block ‘User HVAC Room Settings’ shall provide the system with the following settings and show the current information:

 - absolute user temperature setpoint (°C)
 - relative user temperature setpoint (K)
 - comfort prolongation
 - comfort pushbutton
 - HVAC mode
 - Fan speed settings and current fan speed

 The selection out of these functions is implementation specific.

 This Functional Block is used e.g., in a ‘Room Device’ or in a more complex device that has one or some of these functions.

##### 4.1.2 Existing FBs

###### • User HVAC Room Settings (UHRS) (Chapter 7/10/2 ([02]) clause 3.2)
 • User HVAC Display (UHD) (Chapter 7/10/2 ([02]) clause 3.3)
 • Room Temperature Setpoint Absolute Setting (RTSA) (Chapter 7/10/2 ([02]) clause 3.9)
 • User Fan Speed Setting (UFS) (Chapter 7/10/2 ([02]) clause 3.5)

##### 4.1.3 Functional specification
###### The distribution of the setpoint information in the system is event driven. (COV-condition, change of value) and in addition repeated periodically.

##### 4.1.4 Contraints
###### None.

4.1.7.2.2 Input TempRoomSetpUserAbsEff

DP Name: TempRoomSetpUserAbsEff Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: UHRS
**Description**
Effective absolute temperature setpoint from the RTSM.
This is the value that the RTSM will use as effective value for the user temperature setpoint. It may b
different from the value that the UHRS requested via the Output TempRoomSetpUserAbs, for various
reasons, but also if there is more than one UHRS in the control zone.
Additionally, this Input TempRoomSetpUserAbsEff allows that, in case there are multiple devices with
UHRS in a control zone, that the displays of these devices show the same user setpoint.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_Value_Temp
DPT Format: F16 DPT_ID: 9.001
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
FloatValue This field shall contain the absolute temperature M full °C none
setpoint from the RTSM.

**Access Type**
♦ Input
N → this 1 → this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out: 31 min (rec.)
Request Polling: Period:
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.

Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):

None.
**Special Features**

###### 4.1.7.6 Outputs - HVACmode

4.1.7.6.1 Output HVACModeUser

DP Name: HVACModeUser Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: UHRS
**Description**
This Output contains value of the user defined HVAC mode.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_HVACMode
DPT Format: N8 DPT_ID: 20.102
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
0 ... 4 enum none
**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: MinRepTime: 0 s [a]
Cyclic Period: none [b]
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.

Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
None.
a The signal may be sent immediately if the COV is the result of a user interaction enabling fast
feedback.
b Heartbeat not recommended since a heartbeat causes problems if more than 1 UHRS is linked to
the same consumer and if these UHRS are not synchronized ( toggling of the HVACModeUser at
the consumer).

4.1.7.7.2 Output TempRoomSetpUserOffset

DP Name: TempRoomSetpUserOffset Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: UHRS
**Description**
This information is sent to the FB “Room Temperaure Setpoint Manager”.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_Value_Tempd
DPT Format: F16 DPT_ID: 9.002
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
Full K
**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: 0,2 MinRepTime: 0 s [a]
Cyclic [b] Period: none [b]
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
None.

a The signal may be sent immediately if the COV is the result of a user interaction enabling fast
feedback.
b Heartbeat not recommended, if more than 1 UHRS is linked to the same consumer, since a
heartbeat causes problems if these UHRS are not synchronized ( toggling of the
TempRoomSetpUserOffset at the consumer).

4.1.7.7.3 Output TempRoomSetpSetHeat

DP Name: TempRoomSetpSetHeat Abbr.: (none)

separate data points.

#### 4.2 FB User Presence Switch (UPS)

##### 4.2.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block ‘User Presence Switch’ shall provide the system with the presence information manually entered at a HMI device.

 This Functional Block is used e.g., in a ‘HMI Device’ or in a more complex device that has the corresponding setting functionality.

##### 4.2.2 Existing FBs

###### • User Presence Switch (UPS) (Chapter 7/10/2 ([02]) clause 3.4)

##### 4.2.3 Functional specification
###### The information is transmitted spontaneously at each change.

##### 4.2.4 Contraints
###### None.

### 5 FB Room Temperature Setpoint Manager (RTSM)

#### 5.1 Aims and objectives
###### The FB “Room Temperaure Setpoint Manager” shall provide the HVAC facilities with the necessary temperature setpoints as well as the information about the present and the next operating mode with its delay.

 This information is built from the present and the next HVAC mode, delivered from a supervisor and the local influences given by HMI.

 According to TC247 the following HVAC-Modes are used: Comfort, Standby, Economy and Building Protection.

#### 5.2 Existing FBs

###### • Room Setpoint Manager HVAC-Mode Driven (RSMHD) (Chapter 7/10/4 ([04]) clause 3.4)
 • Room Setpoint Manager Temperature Driven (RSMTD) (Chapter 7/10/4 ([04]) clause 3.5)
 • CH_Room_Regulator_Type_A (Chapter 7/10/11 ([05]) clause 2.7)

#### 5.3 Functional specification

##### 5.3.1 Setpoint temperatures
###### The Inputs TempRoomSetpUserAbs (DPT_Value_Temp, 9.001) and TempRoomSetpUserOffset (DPT_Value_Tempd, 9.002) guarantee compatibility with existing implementations and are therefore mandatory.

 The Inputs TempRoomSetpSetHeat (DPT_TempRoomSetpSetF16[4], 275.100) and TempRoomSetpSetCool (DPT_TempRoomSetpSetF16[4], 275.100) allow a supervisory system to set the current consistent set of setpoint temperatures conveniently in a single Telegram and are therefore mandatory as well.

 The temperature shifts in the Datapoints TempRoomSetpSetHeatShift and TempRoomSetpSetCoolShift shall be added to these setpoint temperatures as given in TempRoomSetpSetHeat respectively TempRoomSetpSetCool; these shall not be added to the common setpoint in TempRoomSetpUserAbs.

##### 5.3.2 Input from more than one Window Switch (WOS)
###### If it is wanted to connection to more than one Window Switch (WOS) sensor, then the Input WOS has to be implemented as many times.

#### 5.4 Contraints
###### None.

#### 5.8 Detailed specification of the Datapoints

##### 5.8.1 Inputs - HVACModes

###### 5.8.1.1 Input HVACMode

DP Name: HVACMode Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description**
This information is provided by a scheduler or a supervisor and defines the actual HVAC operating
mode.
According to TC247 the following HVAC-Modes are used: Comfort, Standby, Economy, Building
Protection.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_HVACMode
DPT Format: N8 DPT_ID: 20.102
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
HVAC Mode 1...4 enum. none
0 = Auto NA
1 = Comfort M
2 = Standby M
3 =Economy M
4 = BuildingProtection M
all other enumeration NA
**Access Type**
♦ Input
N → this 1 → this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out: 31 min (rec.)
Request Polling: Period:
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
None.

###### 5.8.1.2 Input HVACModeNext

DP Name: HVACModeNext Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description:**
This information is provided by a scheduler or a supervisor and defines the next HVAC operating mode
and the time to it. If the next mode is not available the time is set to zero.
According to TC247 the following HVAC-Modes are used: Comfort, Standby, Economy, Building
Protection.
**DPT:** Name DPT_HVACModeNext DPT ID 206.100 Datatype format U16N8
Field Description Sup. Unit Default
Time Time to next HVAC Mode in minutes min 0
0 = no next mode [a]

HVACModeNext enum none
0: No Next Mode [a] M
1: Comfort M
2: Standby M
3: Economy M
4: Building protection M
all other enumeration NA
**Access Type**
♦ Input
N → this 1 → this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out:
Request Polling: Period:
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling:** Save at Powerdown
None.
**Special Features:**
None.
a encoding of special conditions, see table below

###### Interpretation of Time and HVACMode fields

**Time** **HVACMode**

= 0 (Undefined) = 0 (Undefined) [the content of the Datapoint is void / undefined ]

⇒ no next HVAC Mode available for an undefined time period

defined and valid next HVACMode but the delay time is undefined

= 0 (Undefined) = {1..4} (unknown)

⇒ next HVACMode is deactivated

undefined (unknown) HVACMode during a defined delay time

 - 0 = 0 (Undefined) ⇒ in practice this combination is useless and is interpreted like

Time=0 / HVACMode=0 (default value)

 - 0 = {1..4} defined and valid HVACMode and delay time

###### 5.8.1.3 Input HVACModeUser

DP Name: HVACModeUser Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description**
This information is provided by a local HMI and defines the local user operating mode.
According to TC247 the following HVAC-Modes are used: Comfort, Standby, Economy, Building
Protection.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_HVACMode
DPT Format: N8 DPT_ID: 20.102
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
User HVAC 0...4 enum. none
mode 0 = Auto (no manual input) M
1 = Comfort M
2 = Standby M
3 = Economy M
4 = BuildingProtection M
all other enumeration NA

###### 5.8.4.5 Input TempRoomSetpSetHeatShift

DP Name: TempRoomSetpSetHeatShift
FB Name: RTSM
**Description**

(5.8.4.3; see also 5.3.1). The heating values and the cooling values are in separate Datapoints.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_TempRoomSetpSetShiftF16[4]
DPT Format: F16F16F16F16
Field Description
Temperature TempShiftComfort (heating)
Temperature TempShiftStandby (heating)
Temperature TempShiftEconomy (heating)
Temperature TempSetpShiftBProt (heating)
**Access Type**
♦ Input
N → this 1 → this
Spontaneous Cyclically:
Request Polling:
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation:
Saved value:
Transmit on bus (only for output):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**

 - The RTSM can ignore certain values, if they cannot be modified from external (e.g., building

protection setpoint.

##### 5.8.7 Outputs - HVACModes

###### 5.8.7.1 Output HVACModeEff

DP Name: HVACModeEff Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description**
This output contains the effective demanded HVAC mode, manual inputs included.
According to TC247 the following HVAC-Modes are used: Comfort, Standby, Economy,
BuildingProtection.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_HVACMode
DPT Format: N8 DPT_ID: 20.102
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
HVAC Mode 1...4 enum. none
0 = Auto NA
1 = Comfort M
2 = Standby M
3 = Economy M
4 = BuildingProtection M
all other enumeration NA
**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: MinRepTime: 2 s [a]
Cyclic Period: 15 min (recommended value)
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
Support of Datapoint see Functional Block diagram.
**Special Features**
None.
a The MinRepTime of 2 s shall be respected it the COV of the signal is the result of a calculation.

However, the signal may be sent immediately if the COV is the result of a user interaction (locally or
by input signal).

###### 5.8.7.2 Output HVACModeUserEff

DP Name: HVACModeUserEff Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description**
This output contains the effective user HVAC mode, internal and Bus.
According to TC247 the following HVAC-Modes are used: Comfort, Standby, Economy, Building
Protection.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_HVACMode
DPT Format: N8 DPT_ID: 20.102
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
HVAC Mode 0...4 enum. none
0 = Auto M
1 = Comfort M
2 = Standby M
3 = Economy M
4 = BuildingProtection M
all other enumeration NA
**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: MinRepTime: 2 s [a]
Cyclic Period: 15 min (recommended value)
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
Support of Datapoint see Functional Block diagram.
**Special Features**
None.
a The MinRepTime of 2 s shall be respected it the COV of the signal is the result of a calculation.

However, the signal may be sent immediately if the COV is the result of a user interaction (locally or
by input signal).

###### 5.8.7.3 Output HVACModeEffNext

DP Name: HVACModeEffNext Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description**
This output contains the next effective demanded HVAC mode and the time to it. If the next mode is not
available (manual influence etc.) the time is set to zero.
According to TC247 the following HVAC-Modes are used: Comfort, Standby, Economy, Building
Protection.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_HVACModeNext
DPT Format: U16N8 DPT_ID: 206.100
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
Time Time to next HVAC mode in minutes, 0 = no next full min. 0
mode

HVAC Mode 0...4 enum. none
0 = Mode undefined M
1 = Comfort M
2 = Standby M
3 = Economy M
4 = BuildingProtection M
all other enumeration NA
**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: MinRepTime: 10 s
Cyclic Period: 15 min (recommended value)
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
Support of Datapoint see Functional Block diagram.
**Special Features**
None.

###### Interpretation of Time and HVACMode fields

**Time** **HVACMode**

= 0 (Undefined) = 0 (Undefined) [the content of the Datapoint is void / undefined ]

⇒ no next HVAC Mode available for an undefined time period

defined and valid next HVACMode but the delay time is undefined

= 0 (Undefined) = {1..4} (unknown)

⇒ next HVACMode deactivated

undefined (unknown) HVACMode during a defined delay time

 - 0 = 0 (Undefined) ⇒ in practice this combination is useless and is interpreted like

Time=0 / HVACMode=0 (default value)

 - 0 = {1..4} defined and valid HVACMode and delay time

interaction on an HMI. HMI users expect immediate feedback.

##### 5.8.8 Outputs - Setpoint temperatures

###### 5.8.8.1 Output TempRoomSetpUserAbsEff

DP Name: TempRoomSetpUserAbsEff Abbr.:
FB Name: RTSM
**Description**
This output provides the effective absolute temperature setpoint, as RTSM’s result of all
TempRoomSetpUserAbs inputs to RTSM.
This allows that the display of multiple UHRS instances synhronise and show the same user
temperature setpoint.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_Value_Temp
DPT Format: F16
###### Field Description FloatValue This field shall contain the absolute temperature setpoint.

**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value:
Cyclic Period:
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: --**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation:
Saved value:
Transmit on bus:
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
1) No minimum repetition time recommended since change of the value may be caused by user

interaction on an HMI. HMI users expect immediate feedback.

###### 5.8.8.4 Output TempRoomSetpCoolEff

DP Name: TempRoomSetpCoolEff Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description**
This output contains the effective (after corrections) cooling setpoint which is valid for the controller. This
information is used for simple applications (cooling only).

###### 5.8.8.5 Output TempRoomSetpSetHeatEff

DP Name: TempRoomSetpSetHeatEff Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description:**
This output contains the four effective (after corrections) heating setpoints that are valid for the
controller. The heating values and the cooling values are in separate Datapoints.

###### 5.8.8.6 Output TempRoomSetpSetCoolEff

DP Name: TempRoomSetpSetCoolEff Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTSM
**Description:**
This output contains the four effective (after corrections) cooling setpoints that are valid for the
controller. The heating values and the cooling values are in separate Datapoints.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_TempRoomSetpSetF16[4]
DPT Format: F16F16F16F16 DPT_ID: 275.100

### 6 FB Room Temperature Controller (RTC)

#### 6.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Room Temperature Controller (RTC) calculates and controls the position of the valve(s) in order to control the room temperature according to the requested room temperature setpoint.

 The method of calculation of the valve position (setpoint) in the RTC is implementation specific

 For RTC control loop mechanism the current room temperature value, the effective HVAC Mode and a set of room temperature setpoints (for the different HVAC Modes) or the effective Room Temperature Setpoint are mandatory inputs. Additionally, the outside temperature may also be taken into account.

NOTE 1 This FB specification only models the DPs required for Interworking. Advanced control mechanisms
may also take into account information as wind speed, sun intensity or other. These are not modelled in this
document.
###### Optionally the RTC may incorporate local functions like morning boost, start/stop optimization, ECO- function etc. These optimisation functions are implementation specific and not part of the RTC specification.

#### 6.2 Existing FBs

###### • CH_Room_Regulator_Type_A (Chapter 7/10/11 ([05]) clause 2.7
 • HVAC Optimiser (Chapter 7/10/4 () clause 3.3)
 • Heating Individual Room Controller (HIRC) (Chapter 7/11/4 ([06]) clause 2.3)
 • Fan Coil Control (FCC) (Chapter 7/13/1 ([07]) clause 3.2)
 • Water Heat Pump Control for Ringwater (WHPC) (Chapter 7/13/1 ([07]) clause 3.3)
 • Split Unit Control (Basic Part) (Chapter 7/13/1 ([07]) clause 3.4)
 • Radiator and Chilled Ceiling Room Control (Basic Part) (Chapter 7/13/1 ([07]) clause 3.5)
 • Radiator Room Control TU (RRCTU) (Basic Part) (Chapter 7/13/1 ([07]) clause 3.6)
 • VAV Control Discharge Air (VAVCDA) (Chapter 7/13/1 ([07]) clause 3.7)
 • VAV Control Extract Air (VAVCEA) (Chapter 7/13/1 ([07]) clause 3.8)
 • CH_MASTER_FANCOIL_CONTROLLER (Chapter 7/14/11 ([08]) clause 4)

#### 6.3 Functional specification

##### 6.3.1 Room temperature control

NOTE 2 The below is the functional description of one single stand-alone RTC in a room. For the possibility of
having more than one RTC device in a room, please refer to 6.3.4.2 “More than one RTC in a room”.
###### All valves connected to the RTC are controlled together by the RTC. Usually there is only RTC control group per room, i.e. within one room; all valves HVA are usually controlled in parallel. A control group is the combination of an RTC with its linked HVA(s) and FA(s).

##### 6.3.2 Sensors and actuators
###### The RTC uses the current room temperature and optionally the outside temperature for the room temperature control loop mechanism. These sensors may be hard-wired to the device containing the RTC or may be received as external Inputs from the bus.

 If one of these sensors is connected locally to the device containing the RTC, the corresponding Functional Block is activated.

NOTE 3 This FB specification only models the DPs required for Interworking. Advanced control mechanisms
may also take into account information as wind speed, sun intensity or other. These are not modelled in this
document.


-----

###### The RTC controls one or multiple valves HVA. The valves are either hard wired or connected via bus. Within one room, all valves HVA are usually controlled together by the RTC.

 The RTC also controls one or multiple fan actuators FA. These may be hard wired or connected via the bus. Within one room, all fan actuators FA are usually controlled together by the RTC.

 As indicated in convention 2, the FB RTC only foresees one set of DPs for each stage. If in an installation multiple actuators contribute to the same stage, then the integrator shall link these in parallel to the same

 In function of the heating – and/or cooling stages that the implementer of the FB “Room Temperature Controller” intends to control, the following DPs shall be implemented.

##### 6.3.4 Control signals

###### 6.3.4.1 Introduction and overview The RTC may have the control signals, Datapoints, as listed in Table 2 below. All these can be used to switch off or disable the RTC in some way. But they are designed for different purposes and shall be used in the correct way.

 Table 2 – Overview and comparison of the RTC control signals

**Signal**

 - **ContrMode and ContrModeSecondary**

DPT: DPT_HVACContrMode (20.105), N8

Use: To set up a relationship between a Main RTC and one or more Secondary RTCs in
the same control group and make sure that they are working together with a common
goal.

 - **ChangeOverStatus**

DPT: DPT_Heat/Cool (1.100), B1

Use: This indicates whether hot or cold water is provided in a 2-pipe system. It would of
course disable an RTC that can only heat, but that shall be done over its Input
SwitchHeat.

 - **Dewpoint status**

DPT: DPT_Alarm (1.005), B1

Use: To warn the RTC that there is a dewpoint alert and make it adapt its operation.

 - **EnableHeat and EnableCool**

DPT: DPT_EnableHCStage (20.116), N8

Use: This allows an optimizer or a control unit to control the heat stages or cool stages that
an RTC will use. This can be done for performance, time, energy control, costs and
other. It allows disabling all actuators of an RTC, but for that, the ContrMode or the
Switch Inputs should be used.

 - **SwitchHeat and SwitchCool**

DPT: DPT_Enable (1.003), B1

Use: This is the signal that can be used by any control unit, or switch or other, to
completely switch on or off the heating respectively the cooling in an RTC.

###### 6.3.4.2 More than one RTC in a room – ContrMode and ContrModeSecondary In some cases, it is necessary to have more than one control group of valves in the same room (e.g., combined floor heating and radiator heating). In this case two or more room temperature controllers (RTC) are controlling each one control group.

 It is necessary to prevent that one RTC is heating whilst another RTC is cooling. Therefore, there has to be one RTC that decides on whether the room shall be heated to shall be cooled and that passes this information to the other RTC(s). This is called the single “Main RTC” and the other RTC(s) are called “Secondary RTC”.

NOTE 4 The role as “Main RTC” or as “Secondary RTC” is not set via a (standard) Parameter; this follows
from the way how the Inputs and Outputs described below are used.

###### Figure 11 – Multiple RTCs in a single room

 The installer chooses one RTC as Main RTC and links its Output ContrModeSecondary to the Input ContrMode of all Secondary RTCs. For multiple Secondary RTCs the Output ContrModeSecondary has to be implemented multiple times.

 A Secondary RTC shall only heat, respectively cool, if its Input EnableHeat, respectively EnableCool, is set to “Enable”.

 A Secondary RTC has to react properly on not supported value.

 Deadband between heating and cooling

 The control of the Secondary RTCs is done completely by the Main RTCs. Also, the deadband and switching between heating and cooling is contolled by the Main RTC.

 This solution allows that, if the Main RTC is not heating and thus enables the cooling in the Secondary RTCs, that these still may not be cooling, if the room temperature (TempRoom) is according to their settings and Inputs (TempRoomSetpSetCoolEff or TempRoomSetpCoolEff) not too high yet.

 The same obviously applies for a Main RTC that is not cooling: it enables the heating in the Secondary RTCs but does not command it.

 6.3.4.3 ChangeOverStatus The above signals shall not be confused with the Input ChangeOverStatus. This signals (in a 2 pipe system) whether hot – or cold water is provided as a medium and whether thus heating respectively cooling is technically possible. This information is created by the heat – and cold production system and here marked as provided by the Water Changeover Status Sensor (“[WCOS]”).

EXAMPLE 13 If the Main RTC enables the cooling in a Secondary RTC by setting the Secondary RTC Input
_EnableCool to “Enable” but the Input ChangeOverStatus has the value “Heating”, then the Secondary RTC will not_
cool. This situation is However, unlikely, as Main RTC and Secondary RTC in the same room in a 2-pipe system are
typically in the same heat/cold distribution segment, so, it I unlikely that the Main RTC would be cooling whilst the
common medium would be hot water.

###### 6.3.4.4 Dewpoint status The Input DewPointStatus is optional because of the following.

 - It is possible that an RTC operates without dewpoint information, even if its supports cooling.
 - This dewpoint sensor may als be hardwired to the RTC

 The implementation of the Input DewPointStatus is However, highly recommended.

###### 6.8.1.2 Input HVACModeEffNext

DP Name: HVACModeEffNext Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTC
**Description:**
This information is provided by the FB “Room Temperature Setpoint Manager”.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_HVACModeNext
DPT Format: U16N8 DPT_ID: 206.100
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
Time Time to next HVAC Mode in minutes, M min. 0
0 = no next mode [a]

HVAC Mode M 1...4 enum. none
0 = Auto NA
1 = Comfort M
2 = Standby M
3 = Economy M
4 = Building Protection M
all other enumerations NA
**Access Type**
♦ Input
N → this 1 → this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out: 31 min (rec.)
Request Polling: Period:
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling:** Save at Powerdown
None.
**Special Features:**
None.
a Encoding of special conditions: see table below

Interpretation of Time and HVACMode fields

Time HVACMode

= 0 (Undefined) = 0 (Undefined) [the content of the Datapoint is void / undefined ]

=> no next HVAC Mode available for an undefined time period

defined and valid next HVACMode but the delay time is undefined

= 0 (Undefined) = {1..4} (unknown)

=> next HVACMode deactivated

undefined (unknown) HVACMode during a defined delay time

 - 0 = 0 (Undefined) => in practice this combination is useless and is interpreted like

Time=0 / HVACMode=0 (default value)

 - 0 = {1..4} defined and valid HVACMode and delay time

###### 6.8.4.5 Input DewPointStatus

DP Name: DewPointStatus Abbr.: (none)

It is highly recommended that this optional Input be implemented. However, this is not mandatory:
see 6.3.4.4.

###### 6.8.6.3 Input FanManual

DP Name: FanManual Abbr.: (none) Mandatory
FB Name: RTC Can be internal
**Description**
This information is provided by the HMI (UHRS). It shall indicate whether the user wants to manually
control the fan speed or not.
These specifications do not require a time-out foreseen for this Input. This means that if the user
enables the manual control and neglects disabling it again, that the manual control may remain enabled
unnecessarily long. Therefore, it is an implementation specific choice to foresee and enable a timeout or
not.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_Enable
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.003
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
Bit 0: disabled  AUTOMATIC M {0, 1} bit
1: enabled  manual = HMI Value is valid

**Access Type**
♦ Input
N → this 1 → this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out: None[ a]
Request Polling: Period:
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
None.
a No timeout because of compatibility with existing products.

###### 6.8.11.3 Output HeatCoolModeAct

DP Name: HeatCoolModeAct Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTC
**Description**
In this status DP, the FB RTC shall indicate whether it is currently heating or cooling.

NOTE 5 This state Output may differ from the control Outputs EnableHeatEff and – EnableCoolEff. The
current HeatCoolMode cannot always be concluded from the Outputs EnableHeatEff and EnableCoolEff.
EXAMPLE 14 In a Main RTC, the Output HeatCoolModeAct may be “Cooling”, but still its control Outputs
EnableCoolEff to its Secondary RTCs for cooling may be disabled if the Main RTC judges that it has sufficient
cooling capacity and decides not to active another cooling in the room.

**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_Heat/Cool
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.100
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
b 0 = cooling M {0, 1} none
1 = heating

**Access Type**
♦ Output
this → M this → 1
Spontaneous COV: Delta-Value: 1 MinRepTime: 10 s
Cyclic Period: 15 min (recommended value)
Request
**Communication Type**
♦ Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: None.
**Dynamics**
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
**Exception Handling**
None.
**Special Features**
None.

###### 6.8.11.5 Output ContrModeAct

DP Name: ContrModeAct Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: RTC
**Description**
This datapoints shall be used to report the current Control Mode to the UHRS.
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_VHAC_ContrMode
DPT Format: N8 DPT_ID: 20.105
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
ContrMode 0 = not allowed na 0 /..20 enum
1 = Heat O
2 = Mrng Wmup O
3 = Cool O
4 = NightPurge O
5 = Precool O
6 = Off O
7 = Test O
8 = Emerg Heat O
9 = Fan Only O
10 = Free Cool O
11 = Ice O
20 = No Demand O

### 7 FB HVAC ValveActuator (HVA)

#### 7.1 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block ‘HVAC Valve Actuator’ shall contain the functionality for the following "valves".

 - Heating Stage A
 - Heating Stage B
 - Cooling Stage A
 - Cooling Stage B
 - Heating / Cooling for changeover applications

 It is possible to implement only part of this functionality.

 The Functional Block shall translate the valve position setpoint information to the valve position and optionally provide the system with the current valve position as feedback.

 It is also possible to realise an only ON/OFF valve actuator by using only 0 % (0) and 100 % (255). 

#### 7.2 Existing FBs

###### • HVAC Valve Actuator (HVA) (Chapter 7/10/3 ([03]) clause 3.2)
 • CH_Heating_Valve_Actuator (Chapter 7/10/11 ([05]) clause 2.8)

#### 7.3 Functional specification
###### As the distribution of the setpoint information in the system is event-driven  (COV-condition, change of value) and in addition repeated periodically, the input has a timeout.

 Optional functionality

 - Faults in the valve actuator device may be detected and reported.
 - The ActTargetPosHeatStageA etc. may temporary be overridden by means of a tool for service purpose. The ‘Overridden’ condition must be reported.

 Behaviour of the valve if no valid position setpoint is available (company specific)

 - close the valve
 - open the valve
 - leave position unchanged

###### 7.8.2.2 Input ForcedPositionEnable

DP Name: ForcedPositionEnable Abbr.: (none)
FB Name: HVA
**Description**
This input signal enables the forced postition
**Datapoint Type**
DPT_Name: DPT_Enable
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.003
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
Bit 0 = disabled  ActTargetPos is used M 0 / 1 Bit disable
1 = enabled  ForcedPosition is used

N → this 1 → this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out: 31 min (rec.)

Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):

If the timeout occurs, then the default value shall be assumed.
**Special Features**
None.

###### 7.8.4.3 Output CalibrationMode

DP Name: CalibrationMode Abbr.: (none)

This Datapoint may indicate that the actuator is in the calibration mode (S-Mode only); see also Output
CombinedStatus_HVA (7.8.4.5).

### 8 FB Fan Actuator (FA)

#### 8.1 Existing FBs

###### • Fan Speed Actuator (FSA) (Chapter 7/10/3 ([03]) clause 3.4)

#### 8.2 Aims and objectives
###### The Functional Block “Fan Speed Actuator” is designed for simple fan speed actuators.

EXAMPLE 15 In fancoils.
###### It shall receive the fan speed setpoint (ActTargetFanSpeed) and control the speed of the fan from stand still (0 %) to full speed (100 %).

 • If a fan coil is connected of which the mechanics or electronics allow a continuous speed control then the conversion curve from this fan speed setpoint to the rotational speed is implementation specific.

NOTE 6 It is thus not required that there is a linear relationship between the fan speed setpoint (percentage)
and the actual rotational speed.

###### • If a fan coil is connected of which the mechanics or electronics only allow a stepwise speed control then the Fan Speed Actuator shall translate the fan speed setpoint, which is in percent, to the fan step.

 The optional Outputs ActCurrFanSpeed and FanStep shall in both cases be used to provide the current fanspeed as a percentage value respectively as a level.

#### 8.3 Functional specification
###### The percent Input value shall be translated to the fan speed step (100 % divided by the number of steps gives the switch points). The real step position again shall be translated to a percent Output value. This offers a wide flexibility and even works if two devices with different step size are connected (0 % shall always correspond to no fan and 100 % shall correspond to full speed).

 Optional functionality

 • Faults in the fan speed actuator device may be detected and reported in the Outputs “Fault” (8.8.5) and “CombinedStatus_FA” (8.8.7).
 • The ActTargetFanSpeed may temporary be overridden by means of a tool for service purpose.


-----

#### 8.4 Contraints
###### Interworking of devices with different number of steps

 With the coding below combinations of devices with different number of steps is possible. The stop of the actuator is defined and the highest speed of the controller always results in highest speed of the actuator. Steps in between are interpreted to the best.

opened

active

#### 9.2 DPT_CombinedStatus_RTC

 _One year after publication of the Approved Standard version of this paper, this DPT_CombinedStatus_RTC_
_will become mandatory and DPT_HVACStatus (“Eberle status octet”) will no longer be allowed._

1: failure

b1 Active Mode 0: Cool Mode None. {0,1} n.a.
1: Heat Mode

b2 Dew Point Status 0: no alarm None. {0,1} n.a.
1: alarm (RTC locked)

b3 Frost Alarm 0: no alarm None. {0,1} n.a.
1: alarm

b4 Overheat-Alarm 0: no alarm None. {0,1} n.a.
1: alarm

b5 Controller inactive 0: false None. {0,1} n.a.
1: true
(current room temperature
is in the deadband
heating/cooling)

b6 Additional heating/cooling 0: inactive None. {0,1} n.a.
stage (2. Stage) 1: active

b7 Heating Mode Enabled 0: false None. {0,1} n.a.
1: true

b8 Cooling Mode Enabled 0: false None. {0,1} n.a.
1: true

b9-b15 reserved reserved, set 0 None. - None.

#### 9.3 DPT_CombinedStatus_HVA

**Format:** 1 octet: r7B9

octet nr. 2MSB 1LSB

field names

encoding 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 B B B B B B B B B

**PDT:** PDT_BITSET_16

**Datapoint Types**

ID: Name: Use:

22.102 DPT_CombinedStatus_HVA FB

**Field names Description** **Encoding** **Unit** **Range** **Resolution:**

b0 Current Valve position 0: current position=0 None. {0,1} n.a.
1: current position>0

b1 Short Circuit 0: no alarm None. {0,1} n.a.
Note: For thermal drive actuators with a switching contact this does not apply. In this 1: alarm
case this bit is reserved and set to 0.

b2 Overload 0: no alarm None. {0,1} n.a.
Note: For thermal drive actuators with a switching contact this does not apply. In this 1: alarm
case this bit is reserved and set to 0.

b3 Valve kick 0: not active None. {0,1} n.a.
Indicates if valve is moved to protect against blocking of the valve (valve kick) 1: active

b4 Service mode 0: not active None. {0,1} n.a.
Control of the valves over KNX with high priority for commissioning, service and maintenance 1: active
purposes

b5 Manual operation 0: not active None. {0,1} n.a.
(overridden) 1: active
Note: For thermal drive actuators without adirect
manual operation capability this does not apply.
In this case this bit is reserved and set to 0.

b6 Forced position 0: not forced None. {0,1} n.a.
Indicates if valve is moved to forced position. 1: forced

b7 Locked position 0: not locked None. {0,1} n.a.
Indicates if valve control is locked. 1: locked

b8 Calibration Mode 0: not active None. {0,1} n.a.
1: active

b9-b15 reserved reserved, set 0 None. - None.
